page_title: Offsend — One file defines your AI context boundary

summary.name: Offsend
summary.one_liner: Offsend is an open-source, local-first boundary layer that controls what AI coding agents can see, using a committed .offsend.yml file, local secret sealing, and runtime hooks for Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, and Codex.
keywords: keep secrets out of ai prompts
use_cases: keep secrets out of AI coding agent context
enforce AI ignore rules across a repository
gate prompts, file reads and shell commands for coding agents
scan staged diffs for keys and tokens in CI
restore sealed secrets in agent replies
summary.what_it_does: Offsend is a local CLI that defines an AI context boundary for a repository. A committed .offsend.yml holds team policy, and offsend sync generates AI ignore files and installs supported editor hooks. Runtime gates check prompts, file reads, writes, shell commands and MCP arguments on editors that expose those hooks. On Cursor and Claude Code it can seal secret values in MCP responses into reversible tokens, which offsend unseal restores locally. It also includes offsend check for scanning files, staged diffs and stdin for secret-like patterns, and a CI mode (check --policy) for a GitHub Action.
notable: Seals secrets into reversible tokens so the agent keeps working without plaintext
Per-editor gate coverage: Cursor and Claude Code full, Windsurf without MCP response seal, Codex prompt-only
Three layers: machine-level hooks, repo .offsend.yml, and CI check --policy
Local-first; CLI checks run locally and no cloud scanning is required
caveats: Defense-in-depth only, not a guarantee that an agent cannot read a file
Codex has no file or MCP gates yet; Windsurf cannot seal MCP responses; cloud agent sessions are outside local hooks
Not a full git-history secret scanner; use alongside Gitleaks, TruffleHog or GitHub secret scanning for deep history coverage
